children: BEFORE THE BELL: EUROPE WEAKER, ENERGY STOCKS UP

European futures fell on Monday as fresh fighting between the U.S. and Iran boosted oil prices and helped drive bond yields to new multi-year highs after hawkish comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday raised the likelihood of policy tightening.
While London markets
CURRENCYCOM:UK100
were shut for a holiday, likely reducing activity, Euro STOXX 50
and DAX
futures fell around 0.2%, while tech-heavy Nasdaq contracts
traded little changed.

Escalating Middle East tensions and surging bond yields capped an otherwise positive month for global stocks, underpinned by one of the strongest earnings seasons in years and renewed optimism around the artificial intelligence trade.
Europe's STOXX 600
is up almost 1% so far in August and is on track for its fifth consecutive month of gains.
According to CME's FedWatch tool, markets are pricing in roughly a 60% chance of a quarter-point rate hike at next month's meeting, compared with around 40% before Warsh's speech.
Corporate news in the region was sparse.
Energy stocks (.SXEP) rose in premarket trading and were set to help limit losses at the open. TotalEnergies
and Eni
were among the top blue chip gainers on Tradegate, up around 0.7%, as Brent prices
surged above $90 a barrel.
Defence group Rheinmetall
added 1%, while software maker SAP
fell 1%.
